data.title: Flucytosine (5-FC)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antifungals_

**Class:** Fluorinated pyrimidine antifungal

## Mechanism of action
- Taken up by fungal cytosine permease and converted by cytosine deaminase (absent in human cells) to 5-fluorouracil
- 5-FU inhibits thymidylate synthase and is incorporated into fungal RNA
- Rapid resistance when used alone — always combined

## Pharmacokinetics
- Well absorbed; excellent CSF penetration; renal excretion (adjust dose)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cryptococcal meningitis (induction with amphotericin B or fluconazole)
- Chromoblastomycosis (with itraconazole/amphotericin B)
- Severe candidiasis (with amphotericin B)

## Dose & formulations
- 100 mg/kg/day orally in 4 divided doses (adjust to renal function and serum levels)

## Adverse effects
- Bone marrow suppression (leucopenia, thrombocytopenia), especially with renal failure
- Hepatotoxicity, GI upset (enterocolitis)

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy; severe marrow suppression

## Drug interactions
- Amphotericin B reduces its renal clearance (synergy but toxicity); cytosine arabinoside antagonises

## Monitoring
- CBC, LFT, renal function; drug levels where available

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (teratogenic in animals; converted to 5-FU).

## Viva points
- Prodrug converted to 5-FU only in fungi (cytosine deaminase)
- Never used alone — resistance
- Chromoblastomycosis and cryptococcal meningitis

_Sources: Khopkar ch.2; Wolverton 4e ch.10. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
